question: Can EcoDispatch represent an incident as a bundle of heterogeneous resources with independent availability rather than one fire consuming one modeled brigade?

scope.historical_demand: inherit the frozen 2006-2023 EGIF cohort from v1.7.1
scope.fleet_reference: INFOCA 2026 Málaga catalogue; this is a present-day structural reference, not a reconstruction of historical fleet availability

evidence_rules.exact_resource_instantiation: requires an explicit unit and base in an official source
evidence_rules.unknown_capacity: must remain null/unresolved; never coerce to zero and never estimate by dividing Andalusia totals
evidence_rules.external_assets: retain ownership/scope and do not silently treat national support as permanently provincial

service_time.status: sensitivity_only_until INFOCA dispatch/withdrawal records are obtained

next_required_evidence: Málaga allocation of specialist groups / support groups / autobombas by base or shift
rules for first-attack bundle composition by incident class and escalation level
outcome_gate: Do not run or publish lambda policy comparisons until the operational resource substrate has enough ground capacity information to avoid a structurally air-only replay.
claim_scope: v1.7.2a validates a multi-resource state/availability architecture against exact published 2026 Málaga aerial assets and explicitly records unresolved terrestrial capacity. It is not an operational performance evaluation.
